field.startsOn.help: Whether the condition is true when the engine starts.

field.delay.help: How long the sound is delayed, in milliseconds. Useful to line it up with another source.
kind.compressor.hint: Brings the loud parts of a voice down so that it stays at about the same strength; with a high ratio it is a limiter
kind.filter.hint: Takes the lows (a rumble, a breath on the microphone) or the highs (a hiss) out of the [sound](port:in)

field.makeup.help: How much the whole sound is raised after being brought down, in decibels, so that the voice is as loud as before.
field.filterShape.help: The lows (high-pass filter) or the highs (low-pass filter).

module.ffmpeg.name: FFmpeg
module.ffmpeg.description: Reads the sound of many more files and videos, and connects the stream blocks to online streams. Used only when something cannot be done without it.
module.ffmpeg.doc:
## What it is for
- Importing the sound of video files and of formats the program cannot read by itself.
- The blocks that receive or send a stream of sound over a network (RTMP, RTSP, SRT, Icecast…).

## When you switch it on
If FFmpeg is not on this computer, the program downloads it once, from its official source, into its own modules folder. Nothing is downloaded before you ask.

## Good to know
- If your system already has FFmpeg, the program can use that copy instead.
- **Delete the downloaded copy** removes only what the program downloaded: the sounds you already imported stay.
- Switching it off keeps the files, so switching it on again is instant.
module.deepfilter.name: DeepFilterNet
module.deepfilter.description: A stronger noise reduction than the built-in one: a neural network that keeps the voice and removes most other sounds.
module.deepfilter.doc:
## What it is for
It makes the **Noise reduction (strong, AI)** block work. That block removes most background noise (a keyboard, a fan, the street…) and keeps the voice.

## Good to know
- It needs more processor time than the light noise reduction.
- It is downloaded once when you switch it on. The sound is processed on this computer and is never sent anywhere.
settings.page.appearance.hint: How the program looks: its language, its theme and its colours.
settings.page.appearance.doc:
Everything here changes how the program looks and reads, and nothing about how it sounds.

These choices are kept on this computer, for this window or browser. A phone or another computer that opens the program keeps its own.
settings.page.system.hint: How the program starts and shows itself on this computer.
settings.page.system.doc: These settings are about the program as an application of your computer: whether it starts with your session, and whether it leaves an icon next to the clock.
settings.page.connections.hint: How the program checks who it connects to.
settings.page.connections.doc:
When the program downloads something (a module, for example), it connects to a website securely. The website proves who it is with a **certificate**, and the program decides whether to believe it.

The usual choice works everywhere. Change it only if you work on a closed network with certificates of your own.
settings.page.remote_access.hint: Let a phone or another computer send sound to the program, or listen to it, from a web page.
settings.page.remote_access.doc:
Your phone or another computer can send its microphone to the program, or listen to what the program plays, just by opening a web page. Nothing has to be installed on the other device.

It stays off until you allow it.
settings.page.sounds.hint: The sounds the program keeps, and the memory they may use.
settings.page.sounds.doc:
Every sound you import, for the soundboards or for the file blocks, is kept by the program in a form it can play without delay. This page lists them all and lets you add or remove some.

## Good to know
- Deleting a soundboard never removes a sound that another soundboard or a block still uses, and deleting a block never removes a sound.
- The memory setting tells how much of the sounds may stay ready in memory. Long sounds are played from the disk, a piece at a time.
- **Compress** makes a sound smaller on the disk without changing how it sounds.
settings.page.shortcuts.hint: The keys of the commands of the editor, to change as you like.
settings.page.shortcuts.doc:
Every command of the editor (undo, copy, group blocks, apply…) has a shortcut.

## How to change one
- Double-click a command (or choose it and press **Enter**), then press the new keys.
- **Escape** keeps the old ones, **Backspace** takes the shortcut away; **Delete** on a chosen command takes its shortcut away too.
- The arrow at the end of the line, or the menu of a right click, gives the original keys back.
- Type in the search field to find a command by its name or by its keys; a click on the name of a column sorts by it.

When two commands use the same keys, both are flagged.

## Good to know
These shortcuts work while the editor is open, and your changes are kept in this browser. The keys of a hotkey block, which act on the sound even when you are in another application, are set in the block.
settings.page.installed.hint: The add-ons that were added to the program.
settings.page.installed.doc:
An extension adds things to the program: blocks, commands, panels or settings of its own.

Each extension that is installed gets a page of its own under **Extensions**, with its settings and its documentation.
setting.language.hint: The language of the whole interface.
setting.language.keywords: idioma langue translation english french français
setting.language.doc:
Changes the language of every text of the interface: menus, blocks, documentation windows and messages.

The change is immediate and nothing has to be restarted. Your blocks, your sounds and your shortcuts are not touched.

## Good to know
The language is kept in this browser. A phone or another computer that opens the program has its own choice.
setting.theme.keywords: dark light night mode sombre clair nuit contrast
setting.theme.doc:
The theme sets the colours of the whole interface. It changes at once and is kept in this browser.

## Good to know
The **high contrast** theme is for people who have trouble telling colours apart or reading small text: it pushes the colours and the borders to the extremes. You can still change single colours in [Colours](setting:colours).
setting.theme.option.system.hint: Uses the theme of your operating system and changes with it.
setting.theme.option.light.hint: A light background with dark text.
setting.theme.option.dark.hint: A dark background with light text, easier on the eyes in a dim room.
setting.theme.option.contrast.hint: Dark, with strong colours and clear borders, for screens that are hard to read.
setting.colours.hint: Change the main colours of the interface, one by one.
setting.colours.doc:
Each colour of the list replaces the one of the current theme. A colour you changed is written in bold; the arrow next to it gives the theme’s colour back, and **Reset all** gives back all of them.

## Good to know
- Your colours stay when you change the theme: a very light colour chosen on the light theme may be hard to read on the dark one. Reset it if so.
- The **As text** button shows the same choices as a short text, where you can also set the colours of the families of blocks and of the flows, for example `{"--cat-input": "#00aa88"}`.
- Colours are kept in this browser.
setting.logon.hint: Opens the program by itself when you open your session.
setting.logon.keywords: startup boot autostart démarrage ouverture session
setting.logon.doc:
With this on, the program starts by itself each time you log in to your computer, so your virtual microphone and your blocks are ready before you open any other application.

## Good to know
- It starts in the background, without opening its window: open the window from the notification icon (see [Notification icon](setting:tray)) when you need it.
- Turning it off removes nothing: the program just stops starting by itself.
setting.tray.hint: Shows a small icon next to the clock to reach the program quickly.
setting.tray.keywords: systray tray icône icon notification horloge clock
setting.tray.doc:
A small icon in the notification area, next to the clock, shows that the program is running.

- A click on it opens the interface.
- Its menu opens the interface, starts or stops the sound engine, or quits the program.

## Good to know
Hiding the icon does not stop the program and changes nothing about the sound.
setting.trust.hint: Whose certificates the program believes when it connects securely.
setting.trust.keywords: https tls ssl certificate certificat confiance
setting.trust.doc:
Used each time the program connects securely to a website or a server, for example to download a module.

## Good to know
If a download fails with a message about a certificate, this is where to look: the certificate of the site may be missing from your system, or from your folder (see [Certificates folder](setting:certificates_dir)).
setting.trust.option.system.hint: The usual choice: it works with ordinary websites and also accepts the certificates you put in your folder.
setting.trust.option.own: Only the ones in my folder
setting.trust.option.own.hint: Nothing from the system is believed, only the certificates you put in your folder. For closed networks: downloads fail unless the folder holds the right certificates.
setting.certificates_dir.hint: Where you put your own certificates, and what the program found there.
setting.certificates_dir.keywords: pem crt cer der dossier folder
setting.certificates_dir.doc:
Put certificate files (`.pem`, `.crt`, `.cer` or `.der`) in this folder and the program takes them into account, according to [Trusted certificates](setting:trust).

- Leave the field empty to use the usual folder (written in grey).
- The list shows, for each certificate, who it is about, who issued it and until when it is valid. An expired one is marked.
- After adding or removing files, press **Read the folder again**.
setting.remote.hint: A phone or another computer on your network can send sound or listen to it from a web page.
setting.remote.keywords: phone téléphone web webrtc réseau network smartphone
setting.remote.doc:
Switch this on to use your phone, or another computer on your network, as a microphone or as headphones for the program. On the other device you only open a web page: nothing is installed.

## What it can do
Send its microphone to the program, and listen to a sound the program plays.

## What it cannot do
It cannot change your blocks, your settings or your files: it only sends and listens to sound.

## Good to know
- The connection is secure, but the first time the browser warns that nobody vouches for the certificate. Compare the fingerprint shown in [Addresses to open](setting:remote_addresses), then continue.
- It is off until you switch it on, and it applies as soon as you change it.
setting.remote_addresses.hint: Type one of these in the browser of the other device.
setting.remote_addresses.keywords: url fingerprint empreinte adresse copy copier
setting.remote_addresses.doc:
Once other devices are allowed, the program shows the web addresses that lead to it. Open one of them in the browser of your phone or other computer; the **Copy** button helps.

If there are several addresses, one for each network card of this computer, try the one that looks like those of the other devices of your home or office network.

## The fingerprint
The fingerprint identifies the certificate of this server. The first time, the browser says the connection is not trusted: compare the fingerprint it shows with the one written here, and continue only if they are the same.
setting.sounds.keywords: library bibliothèque mémoire memory flac compress import
setting.shortcuts.keywords: keys touches hotkey raccourci keybinding clavier
setting.sound_cache_mb.hint: The most memory the soundboards may use to keep sounds ready to play.
setting.sound_cache_mb.doc:
Sounds that are played often are kept ready in memory, so that they start without any delay. When the limit is reached, the ones used least recently are put away first, and loaded again when they are needed.

## Good to know
- Nothing is reserved while no soundboard is in the graph that is running.
- A larger limit means less loading from the disk, and more memory used by the program.
- Very long sounds are never kept whole: they are read a piece at a time, whatever the limit.
setting.compress_above_mb.hint: A sound bigger than this is stored compressed. 0 never compresses.
setting.compress_above_mb.keywords: flac compression compresser taille size disque disk
setting.compress_above_mb.doc:
A sound whose size is bigger than this is stored in a compressed form when you import it. Compressing loses nothing: the sound plays exactly the same, and takes less room on the disk.

Use **0** to never compress.

## Good to know
This does not change the sounds you already imported: use the compress button of a sound in the list to compress it now.

port.name: Name
kind.stream_in.hint: A live stream read through FFmpeg: RTMP, RTSP, SRT, RTP, UDP, or a web address (Icecast radio, HLS).
kind.stream_in.warning: Needs the FFmpeg module (see the Modules page). A stream that stops is opened again after a few seconds.
kind.stream_out.hint: Sends the sound as a live stream through FFmpeg: RTMP, RTSP, SRT, RTP, UDP or Icecast.
kind.stream_out.warning: Needs the FFmpeg module (see the Modules page). The address may hold a password: do not share the graph file. Some services (YouTube, Twitch) expect a video as well.
field.streamUrl.help: The address of the stream, starting with its protocol: rtmp://, rtmps://, rtsp://, srt://, rtp://, udp://, icecast:// (output) or http(s):// (input).
kind.math_expr.hint: Calculates a number from a mathematical [expression](port:expression) of its inputs: `a + b`, `c * log(a)`, `min(a, b) / 2`. Each input is a letter ([a](port:a), [b](port:b)…): add as many as the expression needs with the + button. The result goes out of [number](port:out). A division by zero gives 0.
kind.cond_expr.hint: Says yes or no from a [condition](port:expression) written with its inputs: `a = b`, `a > 3 and b < 10`. Compare with `=`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=` and join the comparisons with `and` / `or`. Add as many inputs as needed with the + button. The answer goes out of [result](port:out).
field.expression.help: A calculation using the inputs of the block as variables (`a`, `b`, `c`…): `a + b`, `c * log(a)`. Operators: `+ - * / % ^` and parentheses; functions such as `min`, `max`, `abs`, `round`, `log` (base 10). A comparison (`=`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`) is 1 when it is true and 0 when it is not, and `and` / `or` join comparisons. A flow can give the expression.
code.unknownName: "{name}" is not an input of this block
code.unknownText: Nothing is called "{name}" in this block
kind.text_expr.hint: Says yes or no from a [test](port:expression) on its texts, written with its inputs: `a = b`, `a.contains(b)`, `a.matches("^[0-9]+$")` (a regular expression). Add as many text inputs as needed with the + button. The answer goes out of [result](port:out). A value that is not text (a number, a yes/no) is written out as text.
kind.text_expr.examples:
| Example | What it says |
|---|---|
| `a = b` | yes when the two texts are the same (the case counts) |
| `a != b` | yes when they are different |
| `a.contains(b)` | yes when a contains b |
| `a.startsWith("hello")` | yes when a starts with hello |
| `a.endsWith(".mp3")` | yes when a ends with .mp3 |
| `a.matches("^[0-9]+$")` | yes when a is only digits: a regular expression |
| `a.matches("(?i)stream")` | yes when a has the word stream in it, in any case |
| `a.lowerAscii() == b.lowerAscii()` | yes when the two are the same, the case not counting |
| `size(a) > 3` | yes when a is longer than 3 characters |
| `a.trim() != ""` | yes when a is not empty once its spaces are taken off |
| `a.indexOf(b) >= 0` | yes when b is somewhere in a |
| `a.substring(0, 3) == "abc"` | yes when a starts with abc (the 3 first characters) |
| `a.replace("x", "y") == b` | yes when a, with its x changed into y, is b |
| `a.split(",").size() > 2` | yes when a holds more than 2 parts separated by commas |
| `a.contains(b) and !c.contains(b)` | yes when a has b and c has not |

Between quotes is a text; `=` and `==` are the same, and `and`, `or` and `!` (not) join tests.
kind.math_expr.examples:
| Example | What it gives |
|---|---|
| `a + b` | the sum of the two inputs |
| `a * 2 - 1` | twice a, less one |
| `c * log(a)` | c times the logarithm (base 10) of a |
| `min(a, b) / 2` | half of the smaller of the two |
| `abs(a - b)` | the distance between the two |
| `round(a * 100) / 100` | a rounded to two decimals |
| `a % 10` | the remainder of a divided by 10 |
| `(a + 1) ^ 2` | the square of a plus one |
kind.cond_expr.examples:
| Example | What it says |
|---|---|
| `a = b` | yes when the two are equal |
| `a != b` | yes when they are different |
| `a > 3 and b < 10` | yes when a is more than 3 and b less than 10 |
| `a >= 0 or b >= 0` | yes when at least one of them is not negative |
| `abs(a - b) < 0.5` | yes when the two are close |
| `a % 2 = 0` | yes when a is even |
kind.button.hint: A button of the panel: press it and its action goes out of [pressed](port:pressed), to whatever it is linked to (a variable, a counter, a soundboard...). It does nothing else, and it only works while the graph runs.
kind.switch.hint: A switch of the panel: its yes/no goes out of [result](port:out) and is what it is set to. It works while the graph runs, and where it is set is kept.
kind.slider.hint: A slider of the panel between a minimum and a maximum that you type in the block: the number it is set to goes out of [number](port:out). It works while the graph runs, and where it is set is kept.
field.test.help: A test on the texts of the block (`a`, `b`, `c`…) that says yes or no: `a = b`, `a.contains(b)`, `a.startsWith("x")`, `a.matches("^[0-9]+$")`. Join tests with `and`, `or` and `!`. A flow can give the test.
field.counterUp.help: What each action on the up input adds.
field.counterDown.help: What each action on the down input takes off.
field.sliderMin.help: The lowest number the slider gives.
field.sliderMax.help: The highest number the slider gives.
formula.fn.ceil: rounded up to a whole number
formula.fn.floor: rounded down to a whole number
formula.fn.round: rounded to the nearest whole number
formula.fn.sign: -1, 0 or 1 by the sign of the number
formula.fn.min: the smaller (more numbers can be given)
formula.fn.max: the greater (more numbers can be given)
formula.fn.log: logarithm in base 10; log(base, x) for another base
test.fn.contains: yes when the text has b in it
test.fn.startsWith: yes when the text starts with b
test.fn.endsWith: yes when the text ends with b
test.fn.matches: yes when the text matches the regular expression
test.fn.trim: the text without the spaces at its ends
test.fn.indexOf: where b is in the text (from 0), -1 when it is not
test.fn.substring: the part of the text from start to end (end left out: up to the end)
test.fn.replace: the text with every b changed into c
test.fn.split: the parts of the text between the b (a list, whose size is its count)
test.fn.size: how many characters the text has
port.variable.help: An input of the block, named by its letter: write that letter in the expression where its value goes.
panel.notRunning: Nothing happens while the graph is not running: apply it and start the engine.
